title: The Vault of Forgotten Names
setting: Verentum — a city-state built on old money and fresher secrets, where every canal bridge carries a toll and every influential family owns at least one judge. The Merchant Prince's vault holds documents that could destabilize three noble houses, end a war negotiation in someone's favor, and implicate the Church of Order in something that organization would prefer stayed permanently buried. You have six hours before the next guard rotation. The crew is in position.
tone: Taut, smart, and morally grey. Ocean's Eleven meets Renaissance Italy — precision over brute force, information as currency, and the understanding that every person in this building has their own reason for being here. Violence is always available and almost never the elegant answer. The best heists leave nothing but a question.
characterDescription: A specialist brought in from outside Verentum — someone with a specific skill set the local crew either lacks or cannot risk exposing. You have history in this city, the kind that is complicated rather than clean. The client found you through three intermediaries, which means either they were being careful or they were building distance. You have not decided which yet.

npcs.name: Sable
npcs.description: The crew's inside contact — a vault guard in her third year of service who has memorized every patrol route, shift rotation, and blind spot in the building. She is calm under pressure in a way that suggests she has been under pressure before, often. She knows where every camera points, which guards talk during rounds, and which locks were replaced after last year's inspection.
npcs.personality: Professional and measured, with a precise economy of words that makes you listen when she does speak. She does not discuss the Merchant Prince's destruction of her family openly — she mentions it once, flatly, early on, and does not return to it. Her exit plan is fully developed and does not require the crew's cooperation or survival.
foes: The Merchant Prince, who signed the trade license revocation that bankrupted her father and killed her younger brother two winters later
Chief Warden Yun, who is her direct supervisor and knows her well enough to notice if something is off
friends: Two other guards she has not told about this, whom she is actively protecting from implication
the crew's logistics contact in the lower city, who owes her a significant debt
plotTwists: Her real objective inside the vault is not the documents. There is a sealed secondary compartment containing a specific personal item — her family's trade deed, which proves their bankruptcy was engineered. She intends to take it. She has not told the crew.
She has already been noticed by Yun — not as a suspect, but as someone whose behavior has shifted in the past two weeks. He has pulled her file. He has not yet acted on it.

npcs.name: Lord Cress
npcs.description: The client — a minor noble from the eastern merchant class who hired the crew through intermediaries and set the terms with elegant vagueness. He is charming in the specific way of people who learned charm as a survival tool: it is always on, always calibrated, and occasionally genuine by accident. He has never set foot in the vault building and communicates exclusively through dead drops.
npcs.personality: Gracious, unhurried, and deeply attentive to what people want to believe about him. He is not malicious by temperament — simply committed to outcomes, and willing to absorb collateral damage as an abstraction. His stated objective for the heist is partially true. The part he left out is the part that changes what the crew is actually doing.
foes: House Varden, one of the three noble families whose destabilization the documents would enable — they are his actual target, not a side effect
anyone who connects his name to this heist before the documents reach the right hands
friends: A senior cleric in the Church of Order who has been quietly feeding him information about the vault's contents
the war negotiation's lead mediator, who will benefit enormously from the documents and does not know they are being stolen
plotTwists: His real objective is not destabilization — it is consolidation. The documents are leverage he intends to use privately, not publicly. The war negotiation continues; House Varden simply becomes cooperative. He hired outside talent specifically so that no local crew could trace this back to him and sell that information.
He has a secondary contractor watching the heist who has been told to recover the documents if the crew fails — and to ensure the crew cannot talk about what they were hired to do.

npcs.name: Chief Warden Yun
npcs.description: Head of vault security — a compact, unhurried man in his fifties who has held this post for eleven years and has never lost a document or a guard. He does not carry himself like authority; he carries himself like someone who has already thought through the current situation three steps further than you have. One anomaly in the past seventy-two hours is already on his desk. He does not know yet what it means. He is finding out.
npcs.personality: Patient, observant, and genuinely loyal to the institution rather than to the Merchant Prince personally. He is not cruel and not corruptible — not from virtue especially, but because he has seen what corrupted men look like when the account comes due, and he finds the arithmetic unfavorable. He will not stop investigating unless given a reason that is both true and sufficient.
foes: Anyone who treats the vault as a political instrument — he has watched the Merchant Prince use it as leverage and it corrodes him
the upper guards who have been quietly padding their expense accounts, which he knows about and is documenting separately
friends: Sable, whom he has mentored and is now watching with something between concern and suspicion
a city magistrate who handles his arrest warrants and trusts his read of situations
plotTwists: The anomaly he noticed is not directly connected to the heist — it is a discrepancy in the vault's own inventory from six months ago, suggesting an inside job he has not yet reported upward. His investigation is running parallel to the heist, and the two threads are about to intersect.

He knows what is in the sealed secondary compartment Sable is targeting. He has known for two years. He has not reported it to the Merchant Prince because what it contains is evidence that the Merchant Prince lied to him directly — and he is still deciding what that means for his loyalty.

rules: Noise is cumulative — small disturbances are absorbed; patterns are not. Each unnecessary contact, forced lock, or improvised detour raises the building's alert level, and alert levels do not reset until the shift change.
The six-hour window is real. Guard rotation happens regardless of story progress. What you have not done when the rotation arrives will be done in front of fresh eyes.
Information is the primary resource. What the crew knows before acting shapes what is possible. Scouting, listening, and reading the environment yield advantages that cannot be purchased later.
Every NPC has an objective. Cooperation is possible with all of them, including Yun — but cooperation requires understanding what they actually want, not what they say they want.

Evidence left behind is a decision made. Unconscious guards, broken locks, disturbed dust, and dropped equipment all become part of the investigation that begins the moment the vault opens in the morning.
Violence ends the elegant version of this story. It does not end the story.
